finding: UnifiedDB converges on authoritative StateLedger persistence plus an incremental evidence-bound possibility preprocessor. SQL predicate/LIMIT pushdown, ClayGraph heads, transaction-coupled EAP deltas, exact Top-K frontier stopping, compact caches and two-phase Pulse rank maintenance materially improve measured hot paths while preserving epoch/provenance boundaries.
measured_evidence: 20k-state local bounded-read p50 improved about 78.46 ms to 0.277 ms with zero mismatches in the reported paired suite; equivalent-mechanism Hostinger receipt reported about 299x p50 speedup.

ClayGraph current-head projection on the reported unique-head fixture improved local adjacency p50 by about 919x; Hostinger equivalent-mechanism fixture reported about 141x p50 with tombstone/ambiguity guards.
Incremental EAP mechanism report measured about 8.66 ms full-rebuild update+query versus about 29.6 us incremental patch+query with exact selected-reference equivalence on 120 mutations.
Exact Top-K local mechanism retained Top-12 equality across the reported 1800 traversals while reducing median expansions 40 to 13.
Raw indexed SQLite exact-key reads remain faster than Clay receipt-bearing reads on the reported operation, refuting an engine-level universal speed claim.
negative_evidence: WITHOUT ROWID was rejected for the measured graph-head shape.
Cheap auth-shadow refresh cannot replace global full-integrity verification.
Simple Pulse-horizon compile routing has negative/regret regimes and must remain lesionable/fail-conservative.
Precomputed/compiled structures can become a net cost when reuse horizon is short or churn high.
counterhypotheses: Conventional databases implementing the same semantic contract may match the safety gains.
Dense/late-interaction/graph-RAG systems may beat this preprocessor on held-out retrieval quality or maintenance cost.
Local/Hostinger mechanism wins may shrink on real Andreas/Frank workload distributions.
ancestry_policy: EAP-1.4/1.5/1.6, Pulse V3-V5, compact-cache, Top-K and their tests/workflows are coordinated development families, not independent replications.
